security_audit.summary: All 36 static alerts are false positives: they match manual setup instructions, documentation syntax, or readable text and test fixtures. The README claims prior Skillstore verification without evidence, which could mislead reviewers into trusting the skill before reviewing it. The README also invites users to enter prompts in an external demo without explaining how it handles the text.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the verification claim unless it links to an independent review of this exact revision. Distinguish marketplace listing from security approval.

remediation.issue: Unclear data handling for the external prompt demo
remediation.suggestion: Explain whether the demo sends or stores entered text. Label the link as optional and tell users to test with nonconfidential prompts.

remediation.issue: Personal workstation paths in published notes
remediation.suggestion: Use repository-relative paths or generic placeholders instead of workstation account names and local source paths.

content.user_title: Write Precise Camera Moves for AI Video
content.value_statement: Vague camera directions can make a video generator guess how to move and where to stop. This skill turns scene goals into prompts with a clear path, pace, and final frame.
actual_capabilities: Select a camera move that supports a specific reveal, change in focus, or story beat.
Write prompts that specify starting and ending frames, camera movement, path, speed, subject framing, and background continuity.
Check whether a reference image shows enough depth, foreground detail, or clear space for the requested movement.
Recommend starting, ending, and intermediate keyframes for shots that cross spaces or change scale.
Identify conflicting instructions and revise the part of the prompt that most likely caused the visible problem.
limitations: The skill writes prompts and plans keyframes. It does not render video, create keyframe images, or run a video generator.
Clearer prompts do not guarantee camera accuracy, subject consistency, or a successful first render.
A single image may not show enough of the scene for a complex camera path.
The skill does not design still images, edit sequences, grade color, or recommend video models.

use_cases.title: Turn a storyboard panel into a moving shot
use_cases.description: Choose a camera move for one story beat. Define what the viewer sees first and what the camera shows at the end.

use_cases.title: Reveal a product without losing label clarity
use_cases.description: Describe a sideways camera move past a foreground obstruction. Specify when the product becomes visible and where its label should remain sharp.

use_cases.title: Repair a shot with background drift
use_cases.description: Compare a failed clip with its original prompt. Change the instruction most likely to cause the drift before testing again.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Slow Push-In
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Draft a single move from a scene description.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write one video prompt for a slow push-in on [subject] in [scene]. Start at [opening framing], keep [subject detail] stable, and stop at [final framing]. Return only the prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Reveal from a Reference Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Use foreground depth to uncover a product.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [reference image] to reveal [subject] from behind [foreground object]. Check whether the image supports a sideways move. Write the path, pace, and final frame, and say what should stay sharp.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Conflicting Camera Directions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Revise a prompt after observing a failed render.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [original prompt] and [visible failure]. Identify the conflicting or missing camera instruction. Rewrite that part only, and name one visible improvement to check in the next render.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Keyframes for a Continuous Move
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Connect two spaces without an abrupt jump.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan one continuous shot from [starting space] through [opening] to [final subject]. Specify the start and end frames and add intermediate frames only where the path needs them. Recommend two shots if the frames cannot support continuous movement.

output_examples.input: Reveal a ceramic bottle from behind a foreground leaf. Keep its label readable.
output_examples.output: Start with a leaf partly covering the bottle. Slide the camera slowly to the right at a steady height. The nearby leaf moves out of view faster than the far wall. Keep the bottle still and its label sharp. Ease to a stop when the entire bottle is visible.

output_examples.input: The camera rises instead of tilting from the planter to the flower. Fix the prompt.
output_examples.output: Keep the camera at a fixed height and position. Tilt upward from the rim of the planter to the flower at a steady pace. Keep the focal length and lighting constant. Stop with the flower centered and sharp.

output_examples.input: Plan a continuous move from a courtyard through a wide doorway to a piano.
output: Start frame: Center the open doorway in a wide view of the courtyard.
Middle frame: Place the camera at the threshold with both sides of the doorway visible and the piano ahead.
End frame: Slow to a stop in a medium shot of the piano. Keep the doorway and furniture aligned across all three frames.

best_practices: Choose one main movement and state what the viewer should notice at the end.
Describe what changes and what stays fixed, including subject position, focal length, or lighting when relevant.
Change one likely cause at a time after reviewing a failed render, then compare the visible result.
anti_patterns: Using mood words such as dramatic or cinematic without specifying camera movement.
Asking for a fixed camera position and a moving camera position in the same instruction.
Adding more adjectives when the shot needs a reference frame or a shorter path.

faq.question: Do I need a reference image?
faq.answer: No. Provide the subject, setting, and shot goal in text. If you have an image, use it to establish appearance and scene layout.

faq.question: Can this skill generate or edit the video?
faq.answer: No. It writes or revises camera prompts and suggests keyframes. Rendering and editing happen in separate tools.

faq.question: How is a push-in different from a zoom?
faq.answer: A push-in moves the camera and changes perspective. A zoom changes the field of view from the same camera position.

faq.question: When should I add an intermediate keyframe?
faq.answer: Add one when the start and end frames leave an important change in space or scale unclear. For example, show the camera at a doorway before it reaches the room beyond.

faq.question: Can it help if my background shifts suddenly?
faq.answer: Yes. Share the original prompt and describe where the shift happens. The skill can suggest a continuity constraint or a better reference frame.

faq.question: Does the prompt work the same in every video model?
faq.answer: No. The prompts describe camera motion in plain language, but video models vary in how they interpret motion and use reference frames.
